paper.title_en: Cyclic universe and uniform rate inflation from polymerized scalar field in loop quantum cosmology
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the uniform rate inflationary universe in the framework of loop quantum cosmology (LQC) and find that this seemingly simple inflationary model is interlinked with various concepts such as cyclic evolution, HNI inflation, and polymer-quantized scalar fields when the background spacetime is loop-quantized. The potential for an \textit{exactly} uniform rate inflation in a loop-quantized FRW spacetime turns out to be a polymerized version of the corresponding potential in general relativity, which mimics the potentials for a polymerized scalar field and hybrid natural inflation (HNI). There is also a radical modification of the background spacetime, leading to a cyclic universe with identical epochs separated by quantum bounces that replace the classical singularity. The energy density and Hubble rate are bounded. Polymerization of the scalar field is found to be intimately tied to the polymerization of the background geometry in LQC. Remarkably, a single polymerized scalar field simultaneously governs the cyclic evolution of the universe and drives the inflationary phase. Preliminary predictions for cosmological perturbations are worked out and are found to depend on the value of the field at the end of inflation. The parameter space is explored to compare the results for the spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio with observational constraints.
